items.hook: The Fall of the West by Owen Jones review – a bracing history of the changing world order
items.body:
A journalist charts a quarter century of geopolitical hubris and economic overreach

Like many Britons born in the 1980s, the journalist and Guardian columnist Owen Jones came of age with Tony Blair’s platitudes ringing in his ears

items.hook: The Archko Volume or Archko Library is a 19th-century volume containing what purports to be a series of reports from Jewish and pagan sources contemporary with Jesus that relate to the biblical texts describing his life.
items.body: The work went through a number of versions and has remained in print ever since. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.

items.hook: Festival do Rio head Ilda Santiago on how Brazilian cinema’s elite profile is fuelling growth
items.body: Fest (October 1-11) will open with Cannes award-winner, Spanish Oscar submission ‘La Bola Negra’.

items.hook: Anglo-Saxons got special treatment in medieval Rome
items.body: A small hoard of medieval English coins found near the Vatican in Rome suggests that early English residents held a privileged status in the holy city

items.hook: Dodsworth is a three-act play by Sidney Howard based on the 1929 novel by Sinclair Lewis.
items.body: Through the title character, it examines the differences between American and European intellect, manners, and morals. Worth a quiet trip down the rabbit hole.

items.hook: Paramount-WBD merger approved; David Ellison names Ynon Kreiz co-CEO
items.body: Merger expected to close next week.

items.hook: Veteran broadcaster Dame Esther Rantzen dies aged 86
items.body: Rantzen, who fronted the BBC's That's Life for two decades, went on to found Childline, and in recent years had been a campaigner for assisted dying.

items.hook: The Urth of the New Sun is a 1987 science fiction novel by Gene Wolfe that serves as a coda to his four-volume Book of the New Sun series.
items.body: Like Book of the New Sun, it is of the Dying Earth subgenre. The world is stranger than it lets on.

items.hook: Out of Shadows is a 2010 children's historical novel by Jason Wallace, published by Andersen Press on 28 January 2010.
items.body: Set in 1980s Zimbabwe, the story follows white teenager Robert Jacklin at a prestigious boarding school as he confronts bullying, anti-black racism, his own morality and the political instability of the time. One of those things you can't un-know.

items.hook: Patrick Radden Keefe’s bestseller London Falling shortlisted for Baillie Gifford prize
items.body:
The acclaimed American journalist, who won the nonfiction prize in 2021, is shortlisted alongside Andrea Wulf and Matthew Sweet

items.hook: At the Back of the North Wind is a children's book written by Scottish author George MacDonald.
items.body: It was serialized in the children's magazine Good Words for the Young beginning in 1868 and was published in book form in 1871. Bring it up somewhere. Watch the reaction.
